passage:
The government should implement stricter gun control regulations to reduce gun violence and protect public safety. While the right to bear arms is enshrined in the U.S. Constitution, it was never intended to be absolute or without reasonable limits. The alarming frequency of mass shootings, domestic violence incidents involving firearms, and accidental gun deaths demonstrates the urgent need for stronger safeguards. Common-sense measures—such as universal background checks, mandatory waiting periods, and restrictions on high-capacity magazines—would not infringe on responsible gun ownership but would make it harder for dangerous individuals to access weapons.  

The argument that "guns don’t kill people, people do" ignores the reality that easier access to firearms escalates the lethality of violent encounters. Countries with stricter gun laws, like Australia and the UK, have seen dramatic reductions in gun-related deaths without eliminating lawful gun use. Public safety must take precedence over unfettered access to weapons designed for mass casualties. Responsible gun owners should support regulations that keep firearms out of the hands of criminals and the mentally unstable. The government has a duty to act—lives depend on it.
